title: Design registry: contribution + deprecation protocol for tokens & components
creator: Mariana Lopes
description: Create and ship a single 'Design Registry' protocol that governs how tokens, primitive components (buttons, tables, charts), and higher-level patterns are contributed, reviewed, versioned, and deprecated. This ticket covers: a) a contribution flow + checklist for submitting changes (design + code), b) an RFC template and minimal review SLAs, c) deprecation taxonomy and timelines for tokens and components, and d) handoff and communication templates for downstream teams and customers.
acceptance_criteria: A documented contribution flow exists in Confluence with step-by-step author/maintainer responsibilities
A lightweight RFC template and example RFC for a token change published and linked from the registry
A review checklist that covers accessibility, visual regression test links, API/props stability, and performance for runtime components
Deprecation categories defined (minor rename, patch, removal) with default timelines and migration guidance for each
A sample deprecation announcement email + console dashboard banner copy and rollout schedule for Dedicated/Private customers
At least one pilot PR + design change (button size token rename) executed using the new protocol with engineering + PM sign-offs
decisions: Adopt semantic component versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where MAJOR increments for breaking changes (API/props), MINOR for new additions/backwards-compatible changes, PATCH for bug fixes

Deprecation policy: 90-day soft deprecation (warnings, docs), 180-day migration window with console banner and changelog, 12-month final removal for components but tokens default to 6-month removal unless high-risk
All token changes must include automated visual regression snapshots and an embeddings-driven usage report (top consumers) before approval
Design RFCs live in Confluence and must link to a GitHub PR and Figma file; review SLA is 5 business days for triage and 10 business days for final sign-off
A small cross-functional 'Design Registry Board' (two designers, two engineers, one PM) will approve MAJOR changes; rotations happen quarterly
